title: Renewal Bill Window for Remittances, NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
## Renewal bill window — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)

For a renewal remittance the insured makes before the term end on a tier that carries no ICC coverage, the bill window is measured from the date the renewal bill was issued — the most recently issued bill for the term starting on this policy's term end — to the day of the remittance, and is 45 days when the policy is mortgage-required, 30 days when it is not, and no days when there is no renewal bill. When the remittance falls outside the window, the remittance before the credits booked with it may not be less than the renewal premium.

| Renewal bill on record | Mortgage-required | Window | Remittance day falls inside when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 45 days | 45 days or fewer after the bill date |
| Yes | No | 30 days | 30 days or fewer after the bill date |
| No | — | No days | Never |

*Hypothetical cases.* On a mortgage-required policy, a remittance 40 days after the bill is inside the window; on a policy that is not mortgage-required, the same remittance is outside it, and the remittance before the credits booked with it is then at least the renewal premium.
